summary: Markets closed Friday's session on an upbeat note after a surprise July jobs loss reshaped Federal Reserve rate expectations. The S&P 500 rose 0.62% to a record 7,757.64, while the Nasdaq Composite surged 1.3% to 26,690.62. Traders interpreted the weaker-than-expected payroll data as reducing pressure on the Fed to hike rates following the contentious July 29 FOMC meeting, which saw three officials dissent in favor of a rate increase—the most divided decision since 2016. Meanwhile, Bitcoin ETFs posted their best week since April, drawing $853 million in inflows following the Coldcard hardware wallet exploit that drained over 7,700 wallets and prompted a flight to regulated custody. Mega-cap tech earnings last week proved a mixed bag: Amazon rallied 17% on strong cloud and operating leverage, while Meta faced scrutiny over capital-expenditure guidance. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's comments about potential progress in talks with Iran on reopening the Strait of Hormuz sent oil prices tumbling more than 5%. July CPI data due August 12 remains the next key catalyst, with FOMC minutes scheduled for August 19 to shed light on the committee's split decision.

signals.title: S&P 500 hits all-time high as surprise July jobs loss cools rate-hike fears
signals.desc: Weaker jobs data reduced expectations for further Fed tightening after the contentious July FOMC meeting, sending stocks to record closes.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs see best weekly inflow since April at $853M after Coldcard wallet hack
signals.desc: The hardware wallet exploit drained $130M from 7,700 wallets, triggering a shift from self-custody to regulated ETF products led by BlackRock's IBIT.

signals.title: Fed remains hawkish as three officials dissent for rate hike in July meeting
signals.desc: The 9-3 vote marked the most divided FOMC decision since 2016, keeping "higher for longer" rate expectations alive despite the hold.

signals.title: Oil drops 5% on potential Iran Strait of Hormuz deal progress
signals.desc: Treasury Secretary Bessent's comments about talks to reopen the Strait sent WTI crude down 5.69% to $75.77 and relieved inflation pressures.

signals.title: July CPI report August 12 becomes critical catalyst after Fed's split decision
signals.desc: Markets await inflation data to gauge whether the three dissenting Fed hawks will gain support for September rate action.

verdict: Markets are extending gains on dovish jobs data, but the Fed's divided July vote and upcoming CPI print on August 12 keep rate uncertainty elevated.
